new_sources.source: Shen et al., On the Diversity of Analogy Making in Large Language Models, arXiv:2608.03233, 2026-08-04
new_sources.projection: Across ten contemporary LLMs, analogy generation shows domain homogeneity; diversity-enhancement methods exhibit a diversity-quality trade-off.
new_sources.rakl_consequence: Scientific JUMP evaluation needs portfolio-level domain-coverage and quality metrics. A set of individually remote analogies can still be collectively homogeneous.

new_sources.source: Liu et al., Serendipity by Design: Evaluating the Impact of Cross-domain Mappings on Human and LLM Creativity, arXiv:2603.19087, 2026-03-19
new_sources.projection: Randomly assigned remote cross-domain mappings did not yield a statistically significant average creativity gain for the tested LLMs, although more semantically distant inspirations had larger effects in both humans and LLMs.
new_sources.rakl_consequence: Remoteness is not sufficient. Preserve the structural-witness gate and do not equate domain distance with useful scientific imagination.

reinforced_not_double_counted: remote association is not sufficient without a structural witness

new_meta_fiber.problem: Candidate-level surface distance does not ensure portfolio-level cross-domain diversity; LLMs can repeatedly select a narrow set of analogy domains, while interventions that increase diversity may reduce quality.
new_meta_fiber.target: Add domain-family coverage, structural-family coverage, redundancy after analogy deduplication, and quality/transfer-validity metrics to the JUMP portfolio benchmark. Compare scalar diversity maximization, Pareto portfolio selection and explicit domain quotas without post-hoc tuning.
new_meta_fiber.falsifier: If matched retrieval systems show no domain-homogeneity or quality-diversity trade-off on the frozen scientific analogy corpus, do not retain extra portfolio complexity solely from external benchmark results.
